description: We are LunarX, a creative and tech-driven team passionate about space, programming, and innovation. We aim to turn complex space concepts into interactive experiences and build something that’s both educational and fun
summary:
Space Mission Design Game is an interactive educational game that allows users to explore the process of designing space missions. Players make mission-related decisions, manage technical constraints, and learn about important concepts in space exploration, orbital mechanics, and mission planning.

The project aims to make complex space engineering concepts more accessible through an interactive and engaging experience.
details: What does your project do, and how does it work? Space Mission Design Game is a browser-based educational game where players take on the role of a Mission Director. In the Mission Planner, players choose between the Moon and Mars and select one of six mission objectives: flyby, orbital insertion, landing, scientific observation, sample collection, or return. They then define a mission budget and contingency reserve. In the Spacecraft Designer, players build spacecraft using catalog components, including engines, fuel tanks, and payloads. Mass, cost, and ideal delta-v update dynamically as the design changes. Delta-v is calculated using the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation. The system reviews the spacecraft design and identifies issues that could prevent launch. In Mission Control, players execute the mission phase by phase while monitoring telemetry, delta-v, resources, risks, and mission events. What are the benefits of your project? The game helps players understand the trade-offs involved in real space mission planning, including objectives, spacecraft design, budget limitations, resources, and engineering constraints. Every displayed value is labelled as one of five categories: Calculated, Simulated, Gameplay, User-defined, or Unavailable. This helps players distinguish between physical calculations, simulated information, game mechanics, and values that cannot be reliably determined. What is the intended impact? Our goal is to make space mission engineering easier to understand without teaching misleading scientific concepts. Unlike simplified space games that may present invented values as scientific facts, our project clearly identifies the source and nature of every displayed value. When accurate trajectory information is unavailable, the game explicitly displays "Unavailable" rather than generating misleading results. What tools, languages, and technologies did you use? - TypeScript (strict mode) - React 19 - Three.js - Zustand - Vite - Tailwind CSS 4 - Vitest - Testing Library The application runs entirely in the browser without requiring a backend server, user accounts, API keys, or specialized hardware. The project includes 1,481 automated tests. Did you use NASA data? The project uses published NASA/JPL reference values for the Sun, Earth, Moon, and Mars, including gravitational parameters, radii, and masses. These reference values are stored in the source code. The project does not use live NASA APIs or external real-time datasets. What makes your project creative and innovative? One of the project's main innovations is its transparent data-labeling system, which identifies whether information is calculated, simulated, based on gameplay rules, user-defined, or unavailable. The simulation also uses seeded random events and command-based time progression. This makes mission runs reproducible and allows players to review the same sequence of events. Instead of pretending to calculate unavailable orbital trajectories, the game openly communicates its limitations. What factors did your team consider? - Scientific honesty: distinguishing real physics from gameplay rules. - Reproducibility: using seeded randomness and command-based simulation time. - Accessibility: keyboard navigation, screen-reader announcements for mission phase changes, reduced-motion support, and text contrast. - Performance: optimizing the 3D scene and preventing unnecessary rendering when it is off-screen. - Maintainability: keeping application screens separate from physics calculations and using automated tests to enforce this structure. What are the current limitations? The game does not simulate actual spacecraft trajectories. Required delta-v values are gameplay values rather than calculated orbital transfer requirements. Currently, players can choose only between the Moon and Mars and operate one spacecraft per mission. Hardware prices and reliability values are illustrative. Accessibility has been checked through automated tests and browser testing, but has not yet been validated with real screen-reader users.
